accepted.evidence: Turner gives European Romani tato 'hot' under taptá, with Pali/Prakrit tatta. The source explicitly prints Zargari tatho for tatto and describes aspiration in place of gemination (p. 127 §2.3.8). Its source-defined tatto variant is already an installed variant, not another assignment row. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner §1 gives Welsh Romani than and Greek Romani tan 'place' under sthā́na. The source prints Zargari thān > tān as an aspiration alternation (p. 127 §2.3.1); the installed tān variant already points to this source form. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner gives European Romani pelo 'testicle' under pēla. The source itself compares Zargari bellu with Early Romani pelo while illustrating medial gemination (p. 127 §2.3.7); the Zargari b- and final -u are retained as attested. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner explicitly gives European Romani guruv m. under gōrūpá, alongside Pali 'bull' and Prakrit 'ox'. The source prints Zargari guruv [guruw] 'ox, bull' and explains its phonetic [w] after /u/ (p. 128 §2.3.20). Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner gives European Romani gudlo/gullo/gulo 'sweet' as derivatives of guḍá² 'molasses'. The source prints Zargari gudlo/guldo with 'sugar; candy, sweet' and explicitly calls this liquid metathesis (p. 129 §2.3.24). The installed guldo variant already points to gudlo; the single reviewed record retains all source senses. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

held.reason: Turner 12511 gives Greek Romani šuzo under *śucya, while 12525 lists the same Romani forms under *śudhya and sends readers back to *śucya. The source only gives Zargari sujjo 'clean' in a gemination example; the precise older branch remains contested.

Turner 14021 hásati supplies regional Indo-Aryan and Nuristani laugh verbs, but no diagnostic European Romani form. The source's Zargari infinitive suffix and stem need separate analysis before selecting a parent.
Turner 5055 places Romani čiv/čhiv 'throw' under chupáti with a kṣipáti crossing. The source's čuv imperative is clear, but the i/u difference and competing ancient root remain unresolved.
